CHAPTER 3: BUILDING REGULATIONS AND LAND USE
3.1 Building Permits
No person shall construct, reconstruct, alter, or demolish any building or structure within the municipal
area without first obtaining a Building Permit from the Town Planning Department. Applications shall be
submitted with approved structural drawings, site plans, and a No Objection Certificate from the fire
department for buildings above four floors.
3.2 Setback and Height Regulations
All buildings shall conform to the setback norms specified in the Development Control Regulations
(DCR). The permissible Floor Space Index (FSI) and height restrictions shall depend on the zone
classification (Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Green) as per the sanctioned Development Plan.
(a) Residential buildings in R1 zones: maximum height 11 metres; front setback 3 metres.
(b) Commercial buildings in C1 zones: maximum FSI as per DCR; fire escape mandatory above 15
metres.
3.3 Unauthorized Constructions
Any building or part thereof constructed without a valid permit, or in deviation from the sanctioned plan,
shall be deemed an unauthorized construction. The Corporation shall issue a notice requiring the owner
to regularize or demolish the unauthorized portion within 30 days. Failure to comply shall result in
demolition by the Corporation at the owner's expense, in addition to penalties.

CHAPTER 4: PUBLIC HEALTH AND SANITATION
4.1 Solid Waste Management
Every household and commercial establishment shall segregate waste at source into: (i) Wet/Organic
waste, (ii) Dry/Recyclable waste, and (iii) Hazardous/Sanitary waste, and hand over segregated waste to
the designated collection vehicle or bin. Littering on public roads, open plots, or water bodies is strictly
prohibited.
4.2 Drainage and Sewerage
Every building shall be connected to the municipal sewerage system where available. No person shall
discharge untreated sewage, industrial effluents, or construction debris into stormwater drains, rivers,
nallas, or any public water body.
4.3 Prevention of Nuisance
The following acts constitute public nuisance and are prohibited: open defecation, burning of garbage or
plastic in open areas, slaughtering of animals in non-designated areas, keeping animals in a manner
causing health hazard to neighbours, and accumulation of stagnant water that may breed mosquitoes.

CHAPTER 5: WATER SUPPLY
5.1 Water Connections
Every property owner may apply for a domestic or commercial water connection from the Corporation.
The connection shall be granted subject to payment of connection charges, compliance with building
regulations, and availability of water supply infrastructure in the area.
5.2 Water Tariffs
Water tariffs shall be levied on a volumetric basis as measured by water meters installed at each
premises. Tariffs shall be revised by the Corporation periodically based on operational costs and supply
requirements. A minimum monthly charge shall apply irrespective of consumption.
5.3 Prohibited Acts
The following acts in relation to water supply are strictly prohibited:
(a) Unauthorized tapping of water mains or service lines.
(b) Tampering with, removing, or damaging water meters.
(c) Use of a domestic connection for commercial or industrial purposes without appropriate license.
(d) Allowing wastage of water through leaking pipes without timely repair.

CHAPTER 6: ROADS, STREETS, AND PUBLIC SPACES
6.1 Road Maintenance
The Corporation shall maintain all municipal roads, footpaths, bridges, and culverts within its jurisdiction.
Repair of potholes and resurfacing shall be carried out within prescribed timelines as per the Annual
Maintenance Contract. Citizens may report road damage through the Municipal Grievance Portal.
6.2 Encroachments
No person shall encroach upon, occupy, or obstruct any public road, footpath, open space, garden, or
municipal land without written permission from the Corporation. Temporary permissions for events or
exhibitions may be granted subject to payment of fees and compliance with conditions.
6.3 Street Lighting
The Corporation shall provide adequate street lighting on all municipal roads. The Electrical Department
shall maintain a schedule of routine inspection and replacement. Citizens shall not tamper with street light
poles, fixtures, or cables. Theft or damage of street lighting infrastructure is a cognizable offence.

CHAPTER 7: TRADE LICENSES AND COMMERCE
7.1 Mandatory Licensing
No person shall carry on any trade, business, or profession within the municipal limits without obtaining a
Trade License from the License Department. A separate license is required for each premises and each
category of trade. The license is non-transferable without prior approval.
7.2 License Fees
License fees shall be as prescribed in the Schedule of Fees, which may be revised annually by the
Corporation. Fees vary based on the category of trade (food establishment, retail, service industry,
manufacturing) and the floor area of the premises.
7.3 Renewal and Cancellation
Trade licenses shall be renewed annually. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 30 days
before the expiry date. The Corporation may refuse renewal or cancel a license on grounds of
non-compliance with health, safety, or building norms, or on receipt of substantiated complaints from the
public.

CHAPTER 8: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION
8.1 Air and Noise Pollution
No person shall operate any industry, generator set, construction activity, or public address system in
violation of ambient air quality and noise standards prescribed by the Central Pollution Control Board
(CPCB) and the applicable State Pollution Control Board. Noise limits in residential zones shall be 55
dB(A) during day and 45 dB(A) at night.
8.2 Tree Felling
No person shall cut, uproot, or cause irreparable damage to any tree situated on public or private land
within the municipal area without prior permission of the Tree Authority. Permission shall be granted only
in cases of demonstrable public necessity, road widening, or where the tree poses an imminent safety
risk. Compensatory plantation of three trees for every tree felled shall be mandatory.
8.3 Plastic Ban
In accordance with applicable State Government notifications, the manufacture, storage, distribution,
sale, or use of single-use plastic items including carry bags below 75 microns, disposable cups, plates,
straws, and polystyrene items is prohibited within the municipal limits.

CHAPTER 9: BIRTHS, DEATHS, AND CIVIL REGISTRATION
9.1 Registration of Births
Every birth occurring within the municipal limits must be registered with the Birth and Death Registration
Office within 21 days of the event, as mandated by the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, as
amended. The informant shall be the head of household, doctor, or hospital authority where the birth took
place.
9.2 Registration of Deaths
Every death occurring within the municipal limits shall be reported and registered within 21 days. For
institutional deaths (hospitals, nursing homes), the medical officer in charge shall be the primary
informant. A Death Certificate issued by the Corporation is mandatory for all legal and insurance
purposes.
9.3 Issuance of Certificates
Birth and Death Certificates shall be issued by the Registration Officer upon payment of prescribed fees.
Duplicate certificates may be obtained on affidavit in case of loss. Correction of errors in registered
records shall be done through a prescribed application process with supporting documentary evidence.
